title: Magnetic field and magnetic force on moving charges
topicTitle: Magnetic field and magnetic force on moving charges
notes: A charge moving in a magnetic field feels a force q v B sinθ. θ is the angle between the velocity and the field. The force is zero if the charge is at rest or if it moves parallel to the field.
The force is perpendicular to both the velocity and the field. A positive charge follows the right-hand rule. A negative charge is pushed the opposite way.
Because the force is always perpendicular to the velocity, it does no work. The speed stays constant. Only the direction changes.

If the velocity is perpendicular to a uniform field, the path is a circle. The radius is m v / (q B). A faster charge, or a heavier one, makes a larger circle. A stronger field makes a tighter circle.
If the velocity has a component along the field, that component is not changed and the path is a helix. The pitch is set by the parallel speed and the time to go once around.
The tesla is the field in which a charge of 1 C moving at 1 m/s perpendicular to the field feels a force of 1 N. Laboratory fields of a fraction of a tesla already bend electron beams.

Faraday: EMF ε = −dΦ/dt; Lenz's law gives the sign (induced current opposes the change in flux).
Self-inductance L = NΦ/I; inductance stores energy U = ½LI². Mutual inductance M couples two coils.

keyPoints: No force if the charge is at rest.
The force is perpendicular to v.
summary: A moving charge feels q v B sinθ, perpendicular to its velocity, so the speed stays constant. Perpendicular motion is a circle of radius m v /(q B). Motion along the field feels no magnetic force, and a general velocity makes a helix.
